mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive quarterly declines in GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 8.5% within a month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and lower corporate revenue prospects, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above 2.5% for two months signals a monetary tightening in an inflationary environment, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL > 2.5% for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both personal income (PAYEMS) and real retail sales (RSAFS) above their prior six-month average for two consecutive months signals a strengthening consumer demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both exceed prior 6-month average for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS exceed their prior six-month average for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the civilian labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE and rising PAYEMS) over three months signals improved labor market dynamism, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable AND PAYEMS rising for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE is stable and PAYEMS rises for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its trailing 12-month average for six consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer wealth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during six consecutive months where HOUST exceeds its 12-month average.
